81 facts from 39 sources, all accessed on 2026-11-23. 76 are VERIFIED: the quoted passage was found in a primary source (an authority, a ministry, a regulator, an operator or an exchange filing) when the page was re-opened by `scripts/verify_facts.py`. 5 are UNVERIFIED: press reports, or statements that nothing was found. 4 rows carry a CONFLICT note where sources disagree or a later statement supersedes an earlier one.

## NRFF

**F01 (VERIFIED)** Under the New Rail Financing Framework (NRFF) LTA owns the rail operating assets.
- Value: LTA owns operating assets. As of: 2025-05-05.
- Source: [LTA](https://www.lta.gov.sg/content/ltagov/en/who_we_are/our_work/public_transport_system/rail/new_rail_financing_framework.html)
- Quote: "Under the New Rail Financing Framework (NRFF), LTA owns the rail operating assets."
- Note: Page footer: last updated 05 May 2025

**F02 (VERIFIED)** Under NRFF the operator collects fares and pays a licence charge.
- Value: operator keeps fares; pays licence charge. As of: 2021-11-11.
- Source: [LTA](https://www.lta.gov.sg/content/ltagov/en/newsroom/2021/11/news-releases/Transition_of_DTL_to_NRFFv2.html)
- Quote: "Under NRFF, the public transport operator collects the fare revenue paid by commuters and pays the Government a licence charge for using operating assets such as the trains and signalling systems."

**F03 (VERIFIED)** NRFF version one had no mechanism for sharing a fare-revenue shortfall.
- Value: no shortfall sharing. As of: 2021-11-11.
- Source: [LTA](https://www.lta.gov.sg/content/ltagov/en/newsroom/2021/11/news-releases/Transition_of_DTL_to_NRFFv2.html)
- Quote: "Under this first version of the NRFF, the operator bears significant commercial risk as there is no mechanism for the co-sharing of fare revenue shortfall."

**F04 (VERIFIED)** Under NRFF version two LTA shares some of a fare-revenue and profit shortfall.
- Value: shortfall sharing exists; bands not published. As of: 2021-11-11.
- Source: [LTA](https://www.lta.gov.sg/content/ltagov/en/newsroom/2021/11/news-releases/Transition_of_DTL_to_NRFFv2.html)
- Quote: "If ridership turns out much lower than projected and the financials of the operator suffer as a result, LTA shares some of the shortfall in fare revenue and profits."
- Note: No thresholds or sharing rates are given in any source opened

**F05 (VERIFIED)** Under NRFF version two, higher profit-sharing through the licence charge effectively caps operator margins.
- Value: effective margin cap; level not published. As of: 2021-11-11.
- Source: [LTA](https://www.lta.gov.sg/content/ltagov/en/newsroom/2021/11/news-releases/Transition_of_DTL_to_NRFFv2.html)
- Quote: "This also effectively caps the operator’s profit margins."

**F06 (VERIFIED)** Lines placed on NRFF version two in 2016 (SMRT lines) and 2018 (SBS Transit lines).
- Value: NSL, EWL, CCL, BPLRT 2016; NEL, SKLRT, PGLRT 2018. As of: 2021-11-11.
- Source: [LTA](https://www.lta.gov.sg/content/ltagov/en/newsroom/2021/11/news-releases/Transition_of_DTL_to_NRFFv2.html)
- Quote: "The North-South Line, East-West Line, Circle Line and Bukit Panjang LRT were placed on NRFF version two since 2016, while the North East Line, Sengkang LRT and Punggol LRT were placed on NRFF version two since 2018."

**F07 (VERIFIED)** Downtown Line was the first line on NRFF, in 2011.
- Value: 2011. As of: 2021-11-11.
- Source: [LTA](https://www.lta.gov.sg/content/ltagov/en/newsroom/2021/11/news-releases/Transition_of_DTL_to_NRFFv2.html)
- Quote: "The DTL was the first rail line to be placed on the NRFF, in 2011."

**F08 (VERIFIED)** Downtown Line moved to NRFF version two from 1 January 2022 under a single 11-year licence with NEL and SPLRT.
- Value: 11-year licence. As of: 2021-11-11.
- Source: [LTA](https://www.lta.gov.sg/content/ltagov/en/newsroom/2021/11/news-releases/Transition_of_DTL_to_NRFFv2.html)
- Quote: "under a single licence with the other rail lines operated by SBST, North East Line (NEL) and Sengkang-Punggol LRT (SPLRT), with a licence term of 11 years"

**F09 (VERIFIED)** LTA's Annex A rates commercial risk borne by operators as High under version one and Medium under version two; version two licence charge varies with fare revenue and profitability.
- Value: High / Medium. As of: 2021-11-11.

- Quote: "for operators to pay a higher licence charge if profits outperform expectations"

**F10 (VERIFIED)** Licence charges go into the Railway Sinking Fund.
- Value: Railway Sinking Fund. As of: 2021-11-11.
- Source: [LTA](https://www.lta.gov.sg/content/ltagov/en/newsroom/2021/11/news-releases/Transition_of_DTL_to_NRFFv2.html)
- Quote: "The Licence Charge collected from rail operators will go into the Railway Sinking Fund."

**F11 (VERIFIED)** The Railway Sinking Fund is a mix of Government subsidies and licence charges.
- Value: mix of subsidies and licence charge. As of: 2018-11-19.
- Source: [Ministry of Transport, Singapore](https://www.mot.gov.sg/news-resources/newsroom/speech-by-senior-minister-of-state-for-transport-dr-janil-puthucheary-on-second-reading-of-lta-amendment-bill/)
- Quote: "the RSF comprises a mix of Government subsidies and Licence Charge collected from the rail operators under the New Rail Financing Framework"

**F57 (VERIFIED)** SBS Transit to hand over its rail advertising business to LTA from 1 January 2024 as part of the DTL transition.
- Value: 2024-01-01. As of: 2021-11-11.

## Licence term

**F12 (VERIFIED)** NRFF shortened licences from over 30 years to 15 years.
- Value: 15 years. As of: 2022-11-30.
- Source: [Ministry of Transport, Singapore](https://www.mot.gov.sg/news-resources/newsroom/oral-reply-by-minister-for-transport-s-iswaran-to-parliamentary-question-on-ensuring-contestability-in-rail-system/)
- Quote: "one of the changes was to shorten the licence period for rail operators from over 30 years to 15 years today"
- Note: This reply dates the framework to 2016; LTA says the DTL was first placed on NRFF in 2011 (F07). Both recorded.

**F13 (VERIFIED)** Stated rationale for shorter licences: returns for asset-light operators and contestability.
- Value: qualitative. As of: 2026-09-08.
- Source: [Ministry of Transport, Singapore](https://www.mot.gov.sg/news-resources/newsroom/relative-merits-of-periodically-tendering-mrt-operating-licences-versus-having-dedicated-long-term-operators-for-mrt-lines/)
- Quote: "The shorter duration of the rail licences provides the asset-light operators with sufficient returns, while maintaining market contestability to incentivise good performance from operators."

**F14 (VERIFIED)** Licence arrangements are regularly reviewed.
- Value: qualitative. As of: 2026-09-08.
- Source: [Ministry of Transport, Singapore](https://www.mot.gov.sg/news-resources/newsroom/relative-merits-of-periodically-tendering-mrt-operating-licences-versus-having-dedicated-long-term-operators-for-mrt-lines/)
- Quote: "Licence arrangements are regularly reviewed to ensure that they remain fit for purpose"
